title: Sick leave: telling your employer and proof of sickness
version: Employment New Zealand pages 'Taking sick leave' (last modified 7 September 2026), 'Managing sick leave' (last modified 7 September 2026), 'Pay for sick, bereavement and family violence leave' (last modified 7 August 2026), news pages 'Employment Leave Act 2026' (published 7 August 2026) and 'Employment Leave Bill 2026' (published 12 March 2026, update 15 July 2026), all read 20 Nov 2026
sourceNote: Pages from Employment New Zealand, the NZ Government's official employment site. Taking sick leave (for employees): 10 days a year after 6 months (or 6 months averaging 10 hours a week), carry-over to 20 days, telling the employer as soon as possible, sick before or during annual holidays, stress, appointments, part-days, no sick leave left, proof of sickness (under 3 days: employer must ask as soon as possible and pay; 3 or more calendar days in a row: employee pays), pay, ongoing illness, ACC. Managing sick leave (for employers): the same topics from the employer side, plus the 2021 rise from 5 to 10 days and the James/Claire pay examples. Pay for sick, bereavement and family violence leave: otherwise working days, RDP/ADP, part-days (only some sections). Two news pages: only the timing lines. LAW CHANGE: the Employment Leave Act 2026 has passed (news page published 7 August 2026) but does NOT start until 6 August 2028; every page says to follow the current Holidays Act rules until then and 'You cannot start following the new law early'. No page says what will change for sick leave, only that it will change how leave is 'earned, taken and paid'. The topic pages say only 'August 2028'; the older Bill page (12 March 2026, update 15 July 2026) still says the Bill 'is expected to pass this year' (out of date, not wrong for today's rules). News reports (not used for content) agree the Bill passed its final reading around late July 2026. Captured by a fetch tool asked to quote exact sentences; key lines confirmed exact in a second read; small slips in commas and quote marks are possible. Could not be read (fetch permission timed out): the sick leave landing page and the 'Changes to leave coming in 2028' pages. Left out: link-only lists, PDF charts, the remaining parts of the pay page (worked examples, calculating detail). Many link words did not come through and are marked [link words missing], including on the employee page the second option when you have no sick leave left (probably annual holidays, not filled in) and 'paid [ ]' (the employer page says 'paid special leave'). Oddities and gaps on the pages themselves: telling the employer is only 'as soon as possible' and 'should', not 'must'; no page says how to tell them (phone, text, email), how far ahead of a shift, who to tell, or what happens if you do not; the employee page says your employer 'must' ask for proof 'as soon as possible' when you are off under 3 days, but does not say what happens if they ask late; 'less than 3 days' and '3 or more days in a row' leave unclear how non-consecutive days count, and the 3-day rule depends on what the employer 'knows'; 'reasonable excuse' for not giving proof is not explained; 'reasonable period of time' for ongoing illness is not defined; when 'each year' or the '12-month period' starts is not stated; 'dependant' is not defined, and the lists differ (entitlement: 'partners and children, or other dependants'; employee proof: 'spouse, partner, child, or other dependant'; employer proof: 'spouse, partner or dependant', no child); 'can accumulate up to 20 sick days a year' reads as if 20 were a yearly amount, while elsewhere 20 is the maximum balance; the employee page's ACC sentence stops mid-way ('in the form of sick leave or'); the employee 'no sick leave left' list has 'or or' and a stray ', or' bullet; the pay page has 'counted as a using a whole day'; the employee page says your employer 'does not have to agree' to advance, unpaid or special leave unless the agreement says so, while the employer page only says 'you could agree'; sick leave during annual holidays needs the employer's agreement only if you are already on holiday; the James/Claire examples appear without their own heading in the copy. The Jennifer and Holly examples count calendar days, including scheduled days off.
status: Reviewer: 3 instructions missed (incl. who pays for proof depends on when the employer asks), 10 findings, all fixed. 107 of 107 quotes exact (web copy).
